summary: First-order equation solved along its characteristics. Use the slider on the graph to watch the initial profile move.

methods.name: Method of characteristics
methods.reason: The equation is first order and linear in \(u\), so it reduces to ordinary differential equations along curves in the \(x\)–\(t\) plane.

steps.title: Write the characteristic equations
steps.text: Along a curve \(x(t)\) with \(dx/dt = a/b\), the left side of the equation is \(b\) times the rate of change of \(u\). So the PDE becomes two ordinary differential equations.

steps.title: Solve for the characteristic curves
steps.text: Label each curve by the point \(\xi\) where it starts at \(t = 0\). Solving for \(\xi\) gives a quantity that stays constant along each curve.

steps.title: Solve along a characteristic
steps.text: On the curve that starts at \(\xi\), \(u\) starts at \(u_0 = f(\xi)\).

steps.title: Return to x and t
steps.text: Replace \(\xi\) by its expression in \(x\) and \(t\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked by substituting into the equation, and it reduces to f(x) at t = 0.

methods.verify_note: Checked by substituting into the equation, and it reduces to f(x) at t = 0.
